Cameroun Citoyen

An independent civic reference for Cameroon. It matches the written positions of political parties against a voter questionnaire, publishes proclaimed election results with their sources, and maps institutional responsibilities from the region down to the subdivision.

Engineering recordFor technical reviewers

Designed the civic data model and the matching questionnaire, with a strict source policy: every figure dated and sourced, and no party position inferred where none was written.

A citizen answers 24 everyday situations and weights each by importance while party names stay hidden. Scoring compares the answers with each party’s written positions and treats an undocumented topic as unknown rather than as disagreement. Nothing leaves the device.

Key engineering decisions

01

Unknown is not a position

Missing positions are excluded from the score instead of counted against a party, so silence does not distort the match.

02

Privacy by construction

Matching runs in the browser and sensitive attributes are never asked, so there is nothing to protect on a server.

Notes for reviewers

Limits and next stepsResults are covered from 2018 onward; a public changelog of corrections would make the contest channel auditable.
01

Problem statement

Information on Cameroonian parties, elections and institutions is dispersed across party websites, press reports and archives, often undated and unsourced. Electoral choice therefore rests on reputation more than on written positions, and few residents know which authority is responsible for a broken public water point in their street.

02

Contribution

A 24-item citizen profile is matched against the documented positions of 14 parties and reports agreements, disagreements and the topics on which a party has published nothing. Party files can be compared three at a time. Proclaimed results are given with registered voters, valid votes and turnout, and kept apart from contestations. A timeline from 1884, a three-dimensional atlas of the ten regions, constituency pages that set out each official’s competence and help draft a letter, short courses, books and essays in full text, a source library and a daily press digest complete the reference.

03

Architecture

A React client; Three.js renders the regional atlas and PDF.js converts documents in the browser. Questionnaire progress can be saved and resumed. For statutory texts the interface links to Droit Facile.

04

Method and data

Percentages are reproduced exactly as published, and each figure carries its source and date. Party positions are taken from written material only; where a party has published nothing on a topic, the topic is shown as undocumented rather than inferred.

05

Verification and limitations

The public version is still in progress; reading and the questionnaire are open. The comparison can only be as complete as what parties have put in writing, and results are covered from 2018 onward.
